summary: Frontend-only browser verification of self-service password reset/change feature (forgot-password on Login, /reset-password page, ChangePasswordCard in Settings). 4 of 5 test scenarios pass. One real bug found: submitting WRONG current password in ChangePasswordCard causes a spurious redirect to /login instead of showing the inline error (the axios 401 interceptor's auth-endpoint allow-list is missing '/auth/change-password'). Happy path (correct password) works, restore-to-original works, /reset-password without token shows a proper message, forgot-password mini-flow shows the generic 'done' state, and regression smoke login → dashboard still works.

ui_bugs.issue: Submitting WRONG current password causes the axios interceptor in frontend/src/lib/api.js to fire 'aurem:session-expired' and redirect the user to /login, instead of surfacing the inline change-password-error banner. The interceptor's isAuthEndpoint allow-list (lines ~74-80) only exempts /auth/login, /auth/signup, /auth/verify, /auth/resend-verification, /auth/login/2fa-verify, /auth/google — it does NOT exempt /auth/change-password (nor /auth/forgot-password or /auth/reset-password), so a 401 from wrong-current-password is treated as a mid-session token revocation and boots the still-logged-in user out. Reproduced deterministically: on Settings, wrong current pw → page navigates to /login within ~2s and inline error is never visible. The ChangePasswordCard.jsx component itself does set the error state correctly (setError(e?.response?.data?.detail) on catch); the redirect happens because the interceptor dispatches the event before/alongside the component-level catch.

action_items: Fix frontend/src/lib/api.js line ~74-80: add '/auth/change-password' (and defensively '/auth/forgot-password', '/auth/reset-password') to the isAuthEndpoint allow-list so a 401 from these password-flow endpoints is treated as 'inline credential/token error' rather than 'session expired → redirect to /login'.
Optional: also skip the session-expired dispatch when the failing request is same-session self-service auth mgmt (change-password, mfa-*, etc.).
critical_code_review_comments: frontend/src/lib/api.js 401 interceptor: the allow-list of 'inline-error' auth endpoints is enumerated by hand and is missing every new self-service endpoint added in this iteration (change-password, forgot-password, reset-password). Consider inverting the check to an allow-list of paths that SHOULD trigger session-expired (e.g. any /api/aurem-dev/* except /auth/*), so future new auth endpoints default to the safe behavior.
ChangePasswordCard.jsx line 27: minLength check is `next.length < 6` — server-side policy may enforce a longer minimum. Keep client/server rules in sync in one place if possible.

rca of the issue: RCA · Wrong-password redirect on ChangePasswordCard: axios response interceptor in frontend/src/lib/api.js (lines 71-91) treats any 401 that (a) has a token in localStorage and (b) is NOT on a hard-coded auth-endpoint allow-list as a mid-session token revocation, and dispatches window event 'aurem:session-expired' which the app-shell listens for and navigates to /login. The allow-list omits '/auth/change-password'. So when the user submits an incorrect current password: backend returns 401 → interceptor fires session-expired → app redirects to /login → user is logged out and never sees the inline error. Reproduction: login as test@aurem.dev, open /settings, scroll to Change password, enter wrong current pw + any valid new pw twice, click Update password → within ~2s page navigates to /login. Mitigation: add '/auth/change-password' (and '/auth/forgot-password', '/auth/reset-password' for defense in depth) to the isAuthEndpoint allow-list in api.js. One-line fix.
